mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 engine replacement costs typically range from £800 for a used unit to £4,500 for a fully rebuilt engine. Supply-only rebuilt engines average £2,500-£4,500, with supply-and-fit adding £800-£1,200 in labour.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the AJ26 and AJ27 engines in the Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AJ26 (1997-1999) used Nikasil cylinder liners, which were prone to degradation from high-sulphur fuels. The AJ27 (1999-2003) replaced this with traditional iron liners, making it significantly more robust and the preferred choice for replacements.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing the engine is worthwhile if the chassis, interior, and electronics remain in excellent condition. However, with typical market values between £2,000 and £6,000, a full rebuilt engine can represent a large percentage of the car's value.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 engine problems to watch for?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequent issues include Nikasil liner degradation on early AJ26 models, crankshaft pulley harmonic damper separation, and timing chain tensioner oil feed restrictions on AJ27 models.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply-and-fit Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 engine replacement typically takes 2 to 4 working days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components also require replacement.

historyTimeline.h2: Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 launched as part of the X308 generation, it replaced the older 3.2L and 4.0L X300 units, bringing refined aluminium blocks and improved torque delivery to the flagship saloon range. Over its production run, it received a critical revision to address early cylinder lining concerns.

milestones.description: AJ26 4.0L V8 launched (284hp), featuring Nikasil cylinder liners which later proved susceptible to premature wear with certain historical fuel additives.
AJ27 4.0L V8 introduced, featuring revised traditional iron cylinder liners and updated engine management to permanently resolve the Nikasil degradation issue, remaining in production until 2003.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points to help you make an informed replacement decision.

commonProblems.h2: Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 is generally a robust, torque-rich unit, but early AJ26 models are infamous for Nikasil liner failure, while later AJ27 units can suffer from harmonic damper and timing chain issues. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Nikasil Cylinder Liner Degradation - Why the Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 (AJ26) Loses Compression
problems.rootCause: Historical high-sulphur fuels reacted with the Nikasil coating, causing it to flake and leading to rapid bore wear, loss of compression, and heavy oil consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded iron liners or modern coating, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The only permanent fix when catastrophic compression loss has occurred.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 of relevant age is currently valued between £2,000 and £6,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. If the vehicle is worth under ~£5,000, a full rebuilt unit may approach or exceed the car's market value. In these cases, sourcing a low-mileage used AJ27 engine or evaluating the vehicle's scrap/part-ex value is often the most financially sensible route.
problems.recommendation: If your XJ 4.0 V8 is an early AJ26 showing signs of bore wear, a full replacement with an AJ27-spec rebuilt unit is the only permanent fix. For lower-value examples, a verified used engine may be the pragmatic choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt AJ26 Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 engine prices

problems.h4: Harmonic Damper & Timing Chain Wear - Why the Jaguar XJ 4.0 V8 (AJ27) Develops Rattles
problems.rootCause: The rubber element in the crankshaft pulley harmonic damper degrades over time, causing wobble and potential accessory belt failure. Concurrently, timing chain tensioner oil feed pipes can become restricted, leading to chain stretch.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the pulley and upgrading the timing chain, guides, and tensioners.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly suitable as a preventative measure or if caught before catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt engine with all updated components and a 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the timing chain has jumped or caused internal valve damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With typical values between £2,000 and £6,000, a specialist preventative repair (£800-£1,400) is highly viable. However, if internal damage has occurred, the £2,500+ replacement cost risks exceeding the vehicle's value, making a scrap evaluation necessary.
problems.recommendation: Proactively replacing the harmonic damper and timing chain kit on an AJ27 is far more cost-effective than waiting for catastrophic failure. If the engine has already suffered internal damage, carefully weigh the rebuilt engine cost against the car's current market value.
